extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is a bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding in large language models. It comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese), standardized into a unified format for automated evaluation.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench comprises 21 datasets across 6 major task categories: 6 are directly extracted from original datasets, 10 are adapted and processed from existing datasets to suit long context evaluation, and 5 are newly created and annotated (MultiFieldQA-en, MultiFieldQA-zh, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, PassageRetrieval-zh). Data was extracted using random sampling and uniform sampling based on text length.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Literature and film texts (NarrativeQA), scientific NLP papers (Qasper), legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers (ArXiv, C4 Dataset, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, Chinese Government Website), Wikipedia (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en), Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao (DuReader), US Government Accountability Office and Congressional Research Service reports (GovReport), meeting transcripts (QMSum, VCSUM), news clusters (MultiNews, LSHT), web questions (TREC, TriviaQA), dialogues (SAMSum), Chinese sections of C4 (PassageRetrieval-zh), and GitHub code repositories (LCC, RepoBench-P).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Standardized into a unified (Input, Context, Answer) format. For multi-doc QA, supporting passages were combined with distracting passages and randomly ordered up to a maximum length. For few-shot learning, random numbers of examples were sampled from training sets and concatenated into the context. For synthetic tasks, Wikipedia passages and C4 segments were sampled and summarized using GPT-3.5-Turbo or repeated and shuffled. For code tasks, cross-file snippets were shuffled and combined with preceding code lines.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To avoid test leakage, data was extracted from the test sets of public datasets (except VCSUM). TriviaQA passages with less than 1,000 words were filtered out for few-shot examples. In code completion tasks, non-comment generation lines were evaluated. Two extraction strategies were applied: random sampling (main LongBench) and uniform length-based sampling (LongBench-E across 0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+ length ranges).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA (en and zh), annotators were instructed to propose one question and a groundtruth answer for each document with requirements: questions should be clear with definitive, relatively short answers; evidence paragraphs randomly distributed throughout the article; and question types varied (information extraction, summarizing, multi-hop reasoning). The average annotation time per sample was around 5 minutes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators for MultiFieldQA showed a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo was used in the synthetic tasks (PassageRetrieval-en and PassageRetrieval-zh) to generate summaries of sampled passages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: To avoid biases such as 'lost in the middle' where answer-related statements are frequently located at the beginning or end, the placement of evidence paragraphs was made fairly random.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automatic evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect response quality and may underestimate models generating longer responses; performance on LongBench is coupled with the models' instruction-following capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating long context understanding and modeling capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across multi-task and bilingual scenarios.
